title: The funeral
hookLine: Kirtan Sohila and Ardas as the body is cremated
tomorrow: the ashes come home in a box. where do they go?

lines: WHITE CLOTHES, A ROOM OF SINGING.
cards: In movies, funerals are rain, black umbrellas and a long silence. Baba Kartar's is none of those. It's a bright afternoon, people in white and pale colors, and the room is full of singing.
His folder said keep it simple, so it is. The sangat sings the words Simran read to him at bedtime, the same prayer he asked for every night. Then everyone stands, palms together, for Ardas.
Simran opens her mouth to sing with them, and nothing comes out.

teach.b: The prayer is Kirtan Sohila, and here's something to tell a friend tonight: the Sikh goodbye at a cremation is the same prayer Sikhs say before sleep.
The Sikh code of conduct asks for it as the body is cremated, followed by Ardas.
Last week the Sohila's opening showed a wedding day already written, friends at the door. Now the friends are here. The last bedtime, sung by everyone, and a simple goodbye.
Now look back at the week it took to get here. A sparrow at dawn: every creature carries the light. Shaking hands over tea: every season has its work.
An essay, and a story about a truck: ask the elders. A gutka in faded cloth: pass it on. A phone call after a long silence: make peace.
A bed, a window, a friend's hand: sit with them.
Six days, one man, and the same light running through all of it. Simran's voice doesn't come back during the Sohila. The sangat sings it anyway, all around her, and she lets it carry her.

how: At a Sikh funeral the body is cremated while the sangat recites or sings Kirtan Sohila, and Ardas is offered; mourners often wear white or muted colors, and the service is kept simple.

o: a cremation with the bedtime prayer and Ardas
a burial with flowers placed on the grave
a long service with a sermon about the dead

games.q: one week, six lines — tap the pairs.

s: the Sikh prayer at a cremation is a special funeral hymn used nowhere else
it's Kirtan Sohila, the same prayer Sikhs say before sleep.
Ardas follows Kirtan Sohila at the cremation
the Sikh code of conduct asks for the Sohila, then Ardas.
Baba Kartar's family wore white and pale colors.

games.q: a coworker's father has died. she's Sikh and says the family is keeping the funeral very simple. you want to help. what fits?
o: send a huge flower arrangement so the room looks full.
ask if you can come, stand quietly for the Sohila and Ardas, and bring food to the house.
stay away; a Sikh funeral is for family only.
games.why: a simple goodbye: the sangat sings Kirtan Sohila and stands for Ardas. showing up quietly is part of it.

practice: Think of a goodbye you'd want to be simple, for someone you love, or one day for yourself. Count on your fingers the few things you'd want said or sung, and nothing else. Let everything else fall away.

wordCard.voice: The funeral. At a Sikh cremation the sangat sings Kirtan Sohila, the bedtime prayer, and stands for Ardas.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: Kirtan Sohila, the song of praise; the bedtime prayer, also sung at a cremation.

carryVoice: A line to hold: a simple goodbye, sung by the sangat when your own voice won't come. That's the week.
